description:
Adjacent finding surfaced while closing fz-usm.6 (parity audit of the builtin
type-constructor registry).

collect_type_refs (source_publish.rs, ~line 1634) decides which type-position
names become TypeDefined references/waits for a function contract or @type
body. It never consults resolve.rs's CONSTRUCTORS registry or find_constructor
-- it only asks world.reference_type(scope, path, arity), which returns None
for any name nobody in the namespace has bound.

resolve.rs's classify_name checks find_constructor(name) FIRST, before
reference_type -- so a builtin name (list, map, integer, ...) always resolves
to the builtin at *resolution* time, regardless of what the *reference walk*
decided at *publish* time.

Concretely: today, nothing stops a user writing `@type list :: {atom,
integer}` at module scope (reserve_types/note_pending_types, ~line 526, binds
any name including builtin names -- no reserved-word check). Once declared:
- collect_type_refs finds the namespace binding and records a real
  TypeDefined("list", ...) reference/wait for the user's declaration.
- classify_name still matches find_constructor("list") first and silently
  mints the builtin list(any), never consulting the TypeDefined fact the
  publish-time walk just waited on.

The two subsystems disagree about whether a builtin name is "taken" by a user
declaration, depending on which pass touches it. This is the same fragmentation
this ticket is about (three inconsistent name->Ty paths), just not caught by
fz-usm.1-4 because those only touched the resolver, not the reference walk.

Proposed direction (not yet designed/authorized): either (a) collect_type_refs
consults find_constructor first, mirroring classify_name's order and skipping
a ref for a builtin name so shadowing can never look like it did anything, or
(b) reserve_types rejects a @type declaration whose name collides with a
CONSTRUCTORS entry as a clean compile error instead of a silent no-op shadow.
Needs investigation into which reserved-word errors already exist for value
namespace collisions (module/function names) for precedent before picking.

VERIFY: a fixture asserting `@type list :: {atom, integer}` followed by a spec
using bare `list` either errors cleanly or the user's type resolves -- today it
silently resolves to the builtin instead.
title: fz-usm follow-up: reconcile source_publish.rs's collect_type_refs against the resolve.rs CONSTRUCTORS registry
